:::{#rem-cv-estimate}
#### What the cross-validation estimate estimates

Each prediction in @eq-cv-estimate comes from a rule
that did not see the observation it predicts,
so each squared error is scored as in @thm-held-out-unbiased.
But the rule for fold $\fold{j}$ was fitted to $n - \foldsize{j}$ observations,
not $n$,
and the $k$ rules differ from one another and from the rule fitted to all $n$.
So $\cvest{k}$ estimates the [expected generalization error](#def-expected-generalization-error)
of the fitting *procedure* $g$ at the smaller training-set sizes $n - \foldsize{j}$,
which is $\expgenerr{g}{n (k - 1) / k}$ when every fold has $n / k$ observations,
rather than $\generr_{\trainset}$ for the one rule fitted to all the data
[@hastie2009elements, sec. 7.12].

When every [fold](#def-folds) has $\foldsize{j} = n / k$ observations,
$\cvest{k}$ is also the average of the $k$ [fold mean squared errors](#def-fold-mse)
$\foldmse{1}, \ldots, \foldmse{k}$,
the form @james2021islr2e [sec. 5.1.3] use.

:::
